To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
coliform counts were unaffected by composting conditions, but Escherichia, streptococcus, staphylocccus and bacillus counts were affected by composting conditions.
the bacterial counts of coliforms, streptocci, and staphylocci are affected by compost bedded pack moisture content, carbon-to-nutrogen ratio, and space-per-cow.
the C:N ratio, space per cows, and moisture content of the CBP had an effect on bacterial counts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of CBP management on microbial populations.
the effects of composting parameters on bacterial counts.
the effects of composting on bacterial growth and the effects of composted material on bacterial growth in the CBP environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no significant effects of temperature, space per cow or C:N ratio on bacterial counts.

the relationship between compost bed pack performance, management and bacterial counts are not well defined and further research is needed to determine the impact of these variables on the health of the cows.
the relationship between compost bed packed performance, management, moisture, and temperature is complex and not fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C:N ratio and moisture content were the most important factors influencing the microbial population of the bedding material in CBP barns.

coliform, Esch. coli, staphyloccoci and Bacillus spp counts are not affected by compost bedded pack moisture, carbon-to nitrogen ratio, space per cows, ambient temperature or surface and pack depth temperature.
the C:N ratio and moisture of the CBP were the most important factors affecting bacterial counts in CBP barns.
The main takeaway from our work is that
producers can use composting as a means to manage bedding material, but must be cognizant of the conditions under which composting occurs.
the CBP is an effective and economical bedding system for lactating dairy cows.
CBP barns can be used as a management tool for the reduction of mastitis-causing bacteria, but they are not a substitute for other preventative practices.
